what_actual_workflow_already_does_well: Home keeps four useful performance controls visible and directly editable.
One key selects a drum track; one pad changes a step. Running with REC off defaults to selecting without an unwanted extra hit.
All eleven drum tracks and shared accent remain visible against sixteen steps, with selected row, playhead, out-of-length marks and lock notches.
Sound rows keep a stable K5–K8 mapping and fast K2 / repeated PARA navigation. Sparse rows keep the actual physical knob numbers.
Track mute is a modifier chord. Home part mute and pattern cue take one press.
A held step can cross from SEQ to PARA without losing its owner. Edited release preserves the hit; a stopped preview restores base values on release.
Pattern page, length, rate, part selection and pattern selection use separate controls.

count_convention.press: One button, key or pad down plus release. Modifier chords count physical presses separately; a release is already included unless explicitly held.
count_convention.turn: One intended encoder-turn gesture unless explicitly counted as value events. Exact mechanical detents and elapsed time are unqualified.
count_convention.baseline: Starting state is explicit. Do not insert a menu or confirmation that current code does not require. Revised access counts remain unknown until the revised state/control reducer exists.
count_convention.rate_task: Four separated value events describe enumeration distance, not four required turn sessions.
count_convention.correction: The earlier rate row carried4 in a turn-gesture field despite its note. This audit uses4 value events and leaves turn gestures unknown. Some earlier line locators pointed beside their function; this audit supplies corrected exact code locators without changing baseline action counts.

edge_and_light_contracts.contract: SEQ black key selects; default running REC-off suppresses audition; stopped or REC auditions, with local write only SEQ+REC+playing. PARA white key auditions selected sound and never writes a hidden step.

Empty step creates immediately. Existing step is removed only on same owner/pattern/step release <300ms, not created, not used. Long hold keeps it. CHORD+white toggles shared accent. Selection/navigation cancellation prevents old release from deleting another owner.

SEQ→PARA preserves captured held owner; PARA→SEQ while held refuses with RELEASE STEP FIRST. PARA K5–8 lock current typed owner; held K2 probability works only PART/SEQ with no overlay. MIX hold is still step hold, but does not acquire PARA lock/chance scope.

Owner is (target,voice,localID), not Chicago descriptor or knob ordinal. Same underlying drum owner is used from PARA and name-resolved MIX. Held PARA uses lock; normal playing controls use base/motion policy. Release restores appropriate base/live state; do not label MIX held edits p-locks.

Input rejects >=64, not >=current length. Off-loop pad can store a hidden hit without extending loop; LCD grid/pad content masks it outside length. Disabling that route is a new policy, not a retained baseline claim.

Visible MIX kit owns black selection, pad content, track mute, Level/Pan/Rev/Dly target and pad hue. K2/NOTE REPEAT page change does not select global ui.part; K3 part change does follow with matching MIX page. MASTER/WAVE/FX have no drum step pad owner.

Only sixteen white-key logical positions project to RGB pads. Black-key masks are logical, not physical 37-keybed lamps. Pattern/step content and playhead inversion are source-derived brightness states; held ui.keys forces bright after content. REC/WAIT have button roles, not invented normal pad colours.

HOME current909 slot can be bright even empty; occupied slots dim. Empty/END selected SONG row has no current-pattern bright fallback; usedP1 remains dim (dark909 RGB bytes 31,18,5) absent a physically held pad. HOME cue blink only; source has no playing guard on that cue blink.

Normal pad hue selected part except visible drum MIX kit. Bright decoded RGB565 channels >>1, dim >>3; source arithmetic, not measured luminance. SMK plat_glow and plat_play_red are no-ops; no FM-1 redPLAY claim. Clip, calibration and division routes retain distinct existing owners/gates.
